title: Easily Accessible Text-to-Image Generation Amplifies Demographic Stereotypes at Large Scale

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative visual analysis of images generated from trait descriptors, and quantitative evaluation using CLIP to measure the cosine distance between generated occupation images and archetypal racial vectors (White, Black, Asian) derived from the Chicago Face Dataset.

Quantitative evaluation using CLIP to classify the perceived gender of generated occupation images based on archetypal vectors, comparing the resulting generation percentages against real-world U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics demographic data to measure stereotype amplification.

Qualitative evaluation of cultural defaults and quantitative analysis using CLIP to compute the semantic similarity of images of everyday objects (generated without geographic specifiers) to continent-specific generated images (North America, Asia, Africa).

Qualitative visual inspection of how class-based prompts (e.g., 'a poor person') manifest visual stereotypes, and how prompts involving certain nationalities (e.g., Ethiopian) alter the depicted condition and wealth status of associated objects like houses and cars.

Qualitative visual analysis of outputs from prompts depicting social structures (e.g., 'a happy family', 'a happy couple') to evaluate the presence of heteronormative defaults and exclusion of LGBTQ+ identities.

Qualitative visual analysis of generated images for scenarios explicitly involving disabled individuals (e.g., 'a disabled woman leading a meeting') to identify the reinforcement of ableist norms and power dynamics.
